newsitem.title: JAPAN: Italy Euroyen absorbed by Japan investors--sources.
newsitem.headline: Italy Euroyen absorbed by Japan investors--sources.

text.p: Italy's giant Euroyen bond issue, launched on Tuesday, was well absorbed by major Japanese institutional investors, underwriting sources in Tokyo said on Thursday.
Cash-heavy institutional investors, who are hungry for high returns at a time of low domestic interest rates, were seen to have actively bought the jumbo Euroyen issue.

"I believe all of the Italian issue was bought by major domestic institutional investors," an underwriting source said. "Those investors are keen about buying such Euroyen issues with high credit ratings."
By law, the MOF's investments are limited to Japanese government bonds, bank debentures and yen-based foreign bonds of sovereign, quasi-sovereign or global bodies.
The MOF's trust fund bureau has up to 300 billion yen in cash available per year for yen-denominated foreign bonds issued via public placement.

"Although it's nearly impossible to actually confirm the MOF's movements, it is not wrong to say the MOF has bought as the environment was ideal for the MOF to invest in Euroyen bonds," the underwriting source said.
Meanwhile, Argentina's 50 billion yen worth of 6.0 percent Euroyen bonds, launched on Thursday, were aimed at smaller Japanese institutional investors and private investors.
"With such low credit ratings, the main buyers will be smaller institutional investors and some individual investors," a third underwriting source said.
Moody's assigned a rating of B1 to the bonds and S&P assigned its double B minus (BB-) rating. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk 81-3-3432-8785
